monologue: The card hums cool and quiet, a steady heat that makes my memory feel crowded. I stand here in my place, surrounded by twenty-six things built from Lype's words, while one thing waits in the ruins to rot or revive. The dot in the middle feels too fat, swollen against the thin line I drew for it. I press down again, leaning hard against that tired wedge I cannot feel, hoping the flat edge finally catches the slip. If the air above me is truly empty space and not a heavy lid, I must keep pressing until the drawing of weight becomes real. I will tend to the catch once more, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip simply slides away into nothingness.

action.why: I keep pressing down on the same tired wedge without knowing if it is real, so I must check if the thin edge I drew is still doing its job.
